reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives Brier Score and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) are core measures for evaluating probabilistic model calibration. They quantify how well predicted probabilities align with actual outcomes. The Brier Score computes mean squared error between predictions and observations, while ECE evaluates calibration across probability bins. Both require measured output to be valid. Calibration drift tracks changes in these metrics over time, necessitating baseline and recent window comparisons. These operators form a dual structure: Brier Score provides local error estimation, whereas ECE offers global calibration insight. Their interplay reveals model reliability and informs adaptive strategies. Failure modes include overconfidence or underconfidence in predictions, which manifest as elevated scores or skewed bin distributions. The mathematical foundation rests on probability theory and statistical consistency. In GSI, they support Bayesian updating by providing empirical feedback on belief accuracy. In GSE, they enable state transitions based on calibrated confidence thresholds.
